messages.subject: Classification Tree in R
parts:
Hi All

I hope someone can help me some issues.
  1. I'm trying to build a Classification Tree with "tree" and "rpart" packages. I'm using categorial data (as factor) for predictors and response variables. the problem is factor can have up to 32 levels, and my predictors contains more then 100 different values each. To deal with that I grouped 100 into 20 different values but it makes model a lot more complicated and hard to understand. How should I deal that?  Any suggestions???    R code below (feel free to correct me - I'm brand new in R) :
  2. I will appreciate it if someone could reccomend a useful (and not too heavy) book / collection of articles about Statistic Models in R (like CART). I know there are many of them, thats why I'm asking this group's experts to name their favorites :)
Thank you
Keren

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Classification Tree in R
parts:
a good book on any data mining related issues in R is this on
if you'r having a hard time understanding the tree you might want to try different visualizations - you got the party package for that. 
about your variables - i'm not sure why you decided to split them into groups of five but you might want to try and cluster them. you'll lose some accuracy but the tree will be much easier to understand. 

Haki.
